root_cause.text: The `br_nd_send()` function in the bridge neighbor suppression code fails to validate Neighbor Discovery option lengths, allowing a malformed NS packet to cause out-of-bounds reads (advancing beyond the option area) or to use a source link-layer address option that is too small to contain an Ethernet address.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds two checks: (1) `if (!ns->opt[i + 1] || i + (ns->opt[i + 1] << 3) > ns_olen)` to reject zero-length or oversized options; (2) `if ((ns->opt[i + 1] << 3) >= sizeof(struct nd_opt_hdr) + ETH_ALEN)` before reading the source LLADDR, ensuring the option is large enough for the address.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add bounds checks when parsing ND options to prevent out-of-bounds access and ensure option length is sufficient before extracting source link-layer address.
intent_record.what: Added two safety checks: (1) in the loop condition that iterates over Neighbor Discovery (ND) options, a check that the option length does not exceed the remaining option space; (2) before extracting the source link-layer address, a check that the option length is at least the size of the option header plus ETH_ALEN.
intent_record.how: Prevents out-of-bounds memory access and ensures that only valid option data is used for the source link-layer address, avoiding potential crashes or security vulnerabilities from malformed packets.
